posts.name: Prakhar Arora
posts.cooked:
Dear all,

I have talked to many students, few scored 100, few even less than 60, but none complained about mismatch in difficulty between NPPE and OPPE. However, this is personal opinion and no one will judge you for that.

On the web there are many websites, including Leetcode, that offer coding questions on Shell scripting. You can practise your fundamentals but they are in no way going to match the type or difficulty of the questions we have in OPPE.

Plus, the second OPPE is going to be harder to score high marks, it is just meant to help the students pass the subject, so prepare accordingly.

All the best.

Thank you
Prakhar Arora
Teaching Assistant for System Commands

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
Resources are rather very organized for this course particularly.

All the TA sessions with description are available.

  • The ones in Youtube are best recorded sessions (for older terms)
  • The ones shared in the sheet are this term’s TA sessions with resources we shared in the meeting
  • Corrected PYQs are there in Github

posts.name: Agnivesh Jyotiraditya Kannankara
posts.cooked:
To be honest, I will say this. Considering how complicated the OPPE and assignment procedures were in comparison to other courses due to having to be done on the VM, the course team has handled it quite well in my opinion. At least in my experience in this term, there haven’t really been any procedural issues as the SC team have been clear in regards to what needs to be done and how things will work and have been patient and consistent in responding to any queries also.

As for the difficulty concerns, I personally felt the difficulty of the OPPE was in the right spot, not too easy and not too difficult either. Regarding PYQs, I kinda feel that it’s something that’s great if available, but is not something they are required to provide. Particularly since there’s an abundance of practice questions along with their solutions in the course vm regarding the various topics covered. And PYQ s were indeed available if you searched for those too across the various avenues available. Things like that fall into additional research and prep, especially considering the fact that the SC course in particular has both a responsive course team and an abundance of available resources.

Even partially completing the course vm questions should have helped a lot as quite a few of them were tougher than the oppe questions. Considering the vast resources available, even simply searching on discourse for a few minutes could have helped to find the required content.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh

posts.name: Durai Mohandoss C
posts.cooked:
@sayan
I would like to share some feedback about the OPPE experience:

  1. Debugging was quite challenging. It would have been easier if the system showed the expected output vs actual output like other OPPE’s. The red and green indicators were sometimes confusing, and it was hard to understand what to focus on.

  2. NPPE questions were short and easy to understand. But OPPE questions felt very long and a bit confusing. They required more time to read and understand the actual problem.

  3. The Practice and Graded Assignments were available both in the portal and in the VM. Many of us solved them in the portal first and then in the VM, so this part was comfortable not facing much issues.

  4. PYQ files were shared, but not sure how to load them into the VM and solve them. It would have been more helpful if they were directly available in the VM for practice.

  5. Finally, totally underestimated and lacked enough practice from our side due to the overall time constraint.

  6. In future terms, it may be helpful if PPA and GrPA are removed from the portal and students are encouraged to solve everything directly in the VM. This would give more practice and confidence.

Overall it was good learning experience and Thank you for giving us the opportunity to learn.

posts.cooked:
Bro as i remember , hacker rank , leetcode like platforms wont match this, rather you make some small targets to solve with shell script with timer of 2 /3/5 minutes and solve them,

  1. Making triangle with bash script
  2. Making palindrome check and edits
  3. Using awk for sheets analysis like thing , making row and column sums
  4. Trying to implement triangle based fab sequences
  5. Trying to transpose given data with sed

posts.name: Sneha Ramanathan
posts.cooked:
Not everyone is a student here, agreed, but there are a lot of people doing 2 degrees at a time, which is hard to juggle as well and they are still doing well, so are working professionals.

I’ll be honest, I had never worked with linux beyond basic deployment and debugging in AWS before SC. Except for the question on palindrome, I didn’t find any question that was particularly difficult. In fact, I had a semester exam on the 5th, sc oppe on 6th and mlp oppe on 7th. I didn’t have time to prepare fully. I only practiced pyqs and nppe questions and took a crash course on awk and sed.

Additionally, the main thread on oppe had many resources listed and with links provided. It would have taken 5 minutes to go through the thread. If you give the resources to any LLM, they would give you the most important topics and tricks.

BPT and vm extra questions were an excellent indicator of difficulty, in my opinion.
